introduction: Tailored for advanced legal exams, UGC NET, and UPSC Law Optional, this level explores the historic 2026 constitutional amendments designed to reshape the map of India. It analyzes the 131st Amendment Bill, the expiration of the delimitation freeze, and the dramatic federal power shifts between the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.

core_concepts.title: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026
core_concepts.description:
Introduced in April 2026, this bill paves the way for the first true population-based redrawing of electoral maps in half a century.
- Unfreezing Delimitation: The Constitution previously froze seat allocations based on the 1971 census. The 131st Amendment formally removes this freeze, mandating that the upcoming delimitation will be based on the **2011 Census**.
- Expanding the House: The Bill proposes increasing the maximum size of the Lok Sabha from 550 to **850 seats** (up to 815 from states, 35 from UTs), reverting to the principle of strict proportional representation by population.

core_concepts.title: Federal Shift: The Lok Sabha vs. Rajya Sabha Power Dynamics
core_concepts.description:
A profound, heavily tested constitutional consequence of the 131st Amendment.
- The Ratio Imbalance: While the Lok Sabha expands to 850 seats, the Rajya Sabha remains capped at 250 seats (Article 80 is unamended). 
- Joint Sittings (Article 108): The ratio of LS to RS changes drastically from 2.2:1 to **3.3:1**. In any future Joint Sitting, the Lok Sabha's sheer numbers will allow the ruling government to easily crush any opposition from the Rajya Sabha, weakening the Upper House's veto power.
- Presidential Elections: It mathematically dilutes the relative value of Rajya Sabha MPs in electing the President and Vice-President.

core_concepts.title: Telecommunications Act, 2023
core_concepts.description:
Repealed the 138-year-old Indian Telegraph Act, 1885.
- National Security: Empowers the government to take control of, manage, or suspend any telecommunication network during public emergencies (codifying internet shutdowns).
- Satellite Spectrum: Moves away from mandatory auctions, allowing the administrative allocation of spectrum for satellite-based broadband services (a huge shift for space-tech companies).
- Biometrics: Mandates strict biometric authentication for issuing new SIM cards to curb digital fraud.

core_concepts.title: Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act
core_concepts.description:
A paradigm shift toward 'Ease of Doing Business'.
- The Mechanism: It systematically decriminalized minor, technical, or procedural defaults across 42 different Central Acts (including the Environment Act, Pharmacy Act, and Motor Vehicles Act). 
- Civil Penalties: It replaced criminal imprisonment with a regime of heavy financial penalties adjudicated by bureaucratic officers, unburdening the criminal trial courts.

important_entities.name: Delimitation Commission of 2026
important_entities.key_fact: The body tasked with redrawing India's constituencies.
important_entities.significance: Under the newly introduced Delimitation Bill, 2026, this Commission will redraw constituency boundaries to equalize populations based on the 2011 census. Its orders have the force of law and cannot be challenged in any court.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Article 75 caps the Council of Ministers at 15% of the Lok Sabha. With the 131st Amendment expanding the Lok Sabha to 850 members, does the absolute number of allowed ministers increase? **YES**. 15% of 850 allows for a massive Council of up to 122 Ministers (up from the current 81), significantly expanding the Executive.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Remember these three critical data points to navigate any question on the 2026 delimitation reforms.

exam_strategy_tips: In UPSC Mains (GS-2), if asked about the changing nature of Indian Federalism, you must critically analyze how the **131st Amendment (2026)** alters the Article 108 Joint Sitting dynamics, potentially diluting the voice of states represented in the Rajya Sabha.
